output.brief: The enrolment drop is most likely mainly a scholarship effect, not the portal. Yield fell sharply in the Dean's and Merit tiers, where awards were cut (about 13 points each), while the Presidential tier (award unchanged) and the no-merit tier (policy unchanged) barely moved. Early-action admits, whose decisions were processed on the old system, also saw a yield drop of about the same size as regular decision, so the slow portal turnaround does not explain the fall. Applications and admit numbers rose, so a weaker pool is unlikely. The portal's missing-document problem and the slowdown in merit review are still unmeasured. Confidence is moderate: the tier pattern is strong, but it is not a controlled test. Next steps: take the award schedule back to the finance committee with the net-revenue trade-off modelled, before next cycle's award letters go out. Set a regular-decision turnaround target with monthly reporting. Verify the missing-document problem before any vendor action. Do not replace the Admissions Director on this evidence.
